WITH patient_avg_acl AS (
  SELECT 
    p.ID,
    p.SEX,
    AVG(e.`aCL IgM`) as patient_avg_acl_igm
  FROM Patient p
  INNER JOIN Examination e ON p.ID = e.ID
  WHERE e.`aCL IgM` IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX
),
overall_mean AS (
  SELECT AVG(patient_avg_acl_igm) as overall_mean_val
  FROM patient_avg_acl
),
deviations AS (
  SELECT 
    pa.ID,
    pa.SEX,
    pa.patient_avg_acl_igm,
    pa.patient_avg_acl_igm - om.overall_mean_val as deviation_from_overall
  FROM patient_avg_acl pa
  CROSS JOIN overall_mean om
),
sex_avg_deviations AS (
  SELECT 
    SEX,
    AVG(deviation_from_overall) as sex_avg_deviation
  FROM deviations
  GROUP BY SEX
),
final_data AS (
  SELECT 
    d.ID,
    d.SEX,
    d.patient_avg_acl_igm,
    d.deviation_from_overall,
    d.deviation_from_overall - sad.sex_avg_deviation as excess_above_sex_avg
  FROM deviations d
  LEFT JOIN sex_avg_deviations sad ON d.SEX = sad.SEX
  WHERE d.deviation_from_overall > sad.sex_avg_deviation
)
SELECT 
  ID,
  SEX,
  patient_avg_acl_igm,
  deviation_from_overall,
  excess_above_sex_avg
FROM final_data
ORDER BY excess_above_sex_avg DESC
LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: "Missing sex matches nothing" is interpreted as patients with NULL SEX not matching any sex group in the sex_avg_deviations table (using standard `=` comparison where NULL = NULL is unknown), causing them to be excluded from the final result.
The per-patient aCL IgM value is the arithmetic mean of all non-NULL aCL IgM entries for that patient across their examinations. Patients with no non-NULL aCL IgM values are excluded from analysis.
"Missing last" in the ordering refers to handling any NULL values in the excess_above_sex_avg column (though none should exist after the WHERE filter), ensuring they would appear last if present.

alternatives.interpretation: "Missing sex matches nothing" could mean that NULL sex patients form their own distinct sex group (rather than being excluded), and the output should include them but show them last in the sort order. This requires using a null-safe equality operator (e.g., MySQL's `<=>`) in the join to match NULL with NULL in the sex_avg_deviations table.

),

  SELECT
